title: Momentum matrix — weekly KPI scrapbook
content:
Purpose: quick, re-usable weekly scratch where I try to keep momentum on 3 priority outcomes without drowning in metrics noise. Not an org doc — my personal POV and commitments that feed OKR drafts and sprint notes.

Top-level outcome (Q1 draft): Improve inference unit economics on hosted API by 20% while holding P95 latency under 280ms for 1k token median requests.
Why: frees budget for product experiments and helps unlock Dedicated conversations.

Current headline metrics (quick snapshot) — (last 7 days):
- Token cost per 1k (estimated): $0.72   // baseline mid-Jan: $0.90
- P95 latency (median route): 265ms  // target: <280ms
- Cache hit rate (prefix + KV): 31%   // target 40%
- Failed requests (5xx): 0.4%  // unacceptable >0.2%

Momentum matrix (my personal prioritization this week) — 3 rows, quick decisions:
1) Low effort / high impact: tighten batching config on /generate route (product experiment). Owner: me. Hypothesis: small batching window tweaks reduce token cost ~6% with negligible latency regression. Action: deploy A/B config by Wed. Linked ticket: JIRA-PROJ-3421.
2) Medium effort / high impact: KV cache TTL tuning + targeted cache warm for top-10 prompt prefixes. Owner: Mina. Hypothesis: cache hit up to +10pp for top traffic. If effective, scales cost down and improves P50. Action: pair-run with infra on Thu.
3) High effort / medium impact: quantized 8-bit model variants for edge routes. Owner: Eng Research. Longer runway — put on backlog for this sprint but draft rollout plan now.

Weekly check-in (notes-to-self style) — 2026-03-09:
- Progress: batching A/B config implemented in staging; saw 3.8% estimated token cost gain in synthetic bench. Need real traffic test.
- Blockers: feature-flag rollout requires a console change; product-ops backlog slow. Pinged @evan on Slack.
- Learnings: smaller micro-batching window increases variance in P95; need to pair with fallback route for latency-sensitive customers.
- Quick experiment: roll out A/B only to non-SLA routes for 24h, collect token/cost deltas.

Retrospective stubs (things to capture next retro):
- What went well: fast dev turnaround on batching config, good telemetry to compute cost deltas.
- What didn't: missed early stakeholder alignment (CS concerned about latency).
- Action items: create one-pager for CS + simple rollback playbook (me).

Personal OKR draft (copy-to-iterate) — Q1:
- Objective: Reduce unit inference cost to accelerate product experiments.
  - KR1: 20% reduction in avg token spend per 1k tokens across hosted routes.
  - KR2: Maintain P95 latency <= 280ms for median 1k token requests.
  - KR3: Document cost/perf levers and ship 2 automation rules to autopressure fallback when infra signals degrade performance.

Quick notes / scratch reminders:
- Keep the A/B window small at first; avoid racing cache warmers.
- Add a telemetry metric: cost_per_successful_token (to exclude failed/timeout overhead).
- Check with infra: is there a long-tail GC / NVMe flakiness that spikes 5xxs? (ticketed earlier).

Draft email blurb to CS (short):
Hey team — running a low-risk A/B this week to test batching config improvements aimed at reducing token costs. We’re gating the test to non-SLA routes and will monitor P95 closely. If you want early access to the results or to opt out customers, reply here.

Open questions (brain dump):
- If batching reduces cost but increases tail latency for small requests, should we carve small-request routes out or build a latency budget routing policy?
- How to quantify customer-visible UX impact of 10–30ms P95 regressions? (maybe A/B with user-visible metric e.g., conversion rate).

To-do (short):
- [ ] Finish A/B rollout flag + metrics dashboard (TODAY)
- [ ] One-pager for CS + rollback steps (by Fri)
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with Mina + infra for cache warm strategy (Thu)
- [ ] Capture experiment results and add to OKR doc (after 72h of traffic)

Notes to self: keep this doc light; move finished bits into the team OKR sheet or Confluence. Use this as an iterative journal — easy to scan on Monday mornings.

Last quick log: pinged @evan 2026-03-09 09:14 PT — awaiting console change PR review.

-- end --
